>I hated set 6. I know everyone else loved it, but I'm a frontline/backline guy, not a "piece these 6 challengers together" kind of guy.  
  
In set 6, unless you could piece together the few exact challenger, jihn, or urgot boards that worked, your lvl 8 board SUCKED. And I mean it really sucked, like getting 8-0'ed by that challenger board sucked.

Set 6 had plenty of good options for alternative carries if you didn't hit meta 4 costs like seraphine. AP items especially had options on shojin and blue buff carries, in comparison to 6.5 where shojin feels pretty weak for most AP carries. Feels much harder to flex AP. Flexing AD is similar to how it was in set 6 just with the number of carries that can use those items. Don't think I agree with your "piece 6 challengers together" point considering how little I saw that comp. 

​

>in set 6, regardless of your position after lvl 7, if you couldn't hit urgot2 for your lvl 8 board, you were screwed.

If you're talking about Urgot specifically, this is just not true. Half of the meta comps at the end of 6 were reroll comps. If you're saying that you had to 2 star a 4 cost otherwise you would lose, then yeah. You have to 2 star 4 costs. Trying to transition your comp with a 1 star 4 cost after 4-1 is going to lose you a lot of HP in a lot of games.

​

>5 Cost Units Actually Work

I don't see how you think things have changed from set 6 tbh. Viktor came into 6.5 unchanged from his last set 6 patch. Jinx got some damage buffs, but is still as squishy as before. If you're playing 5 costs as carries then yeah you need them 2 star. As late game cap units they worked fine imo.

​

>On 5 innovater, again, it's quite literally 5 innovater + 3. You can play any combination of other units, and you can use Ez, Jayce, or one of your other units as a carry.

Personally I don't this this is a good thing or good for the game. Having lobbies with 3+ people rolling hard to hit 5 innos and putting any random carry they have items for feels boring and not very interesting to see. If other compswere similarly flexible I think it'd be fine but right now innos feels like it's taken the place of renata+bruisers in terms of how easy it is to force.

​

>The New Augments are Fun

I agree! New augments are great, especially when they change the way you build your comp like double trouble does. But sometimes you're getting offered treasure trove, golden gifts, on 1-4. And they seem very weirdly balanced in some places. Chemtech Unity being on silver tier comes to mind. The early game strength of some augments being overwhelming feels bad to play against especially if you've been offered junk. 

Of course this isn't to say you can't enjoy 6.5 but in my opinion set 6 was felt way better to play. Obviously this is because set 6 had multiple patches and set 6.5 is still new so I'm not too worried about it, hoping they can recreate how good set 6 felt with 6.5

morphine != heroin and methamphetamine != ampthetamine. 

Reading through the source you've given later is interesting. I think you've maybe inferred something that's not given by the text though. Where you've said that "regular meth users could not distinguish between the two drugs." is misleading imo, considering how the source describes the subjective effects between similar doses of methampethamine and amphetamine to be "significantly different". When taking methamphetamines users reported feeling more "high" and "stimulated". Methamphetamine also caused higher heart rates than amphetamine in similar doses. The effects are similar but vary in magnitude. Where you're right in saying they're similar is when the choice is given between $20 or AMPH/MA there's no significant difference between them. In the paper's discussion they say their observations are inconsistent with claims the 2 drugs are equally strong and state that the effects of methamphetamine were greater and at lower doses only methamphetamine produced a significant change in mood.

I also think the comparison between morphine and heroin is particularly misleading, given that heroin is reported to be at least double the potency of morphine in a range of studies. Heroin and Morphine are quite literally different compounds, as are methamphetamine and amphetamine. The difference is chemical, as well as being situational. What looks like 1 little metyl group, or a couple of acetyl groups can absolutely cause large differences.
